exposure: maternal serum N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels
cohort: Pregnant individuals with pulmonary hypertension (PH) stemming from mitral valve stenosis, mitral valve regurgitation, or pulmonary arterial hypertension who were admitted to Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital.
finding: Higher maternal NT-proBNP levels are associated with shorter gestational duration and an increased risk of preterm labor in pregnant women with pulmonary hypertension, particularly in those with post-capillary PH.
